Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera are the two openers for Sri Lanka. Chris Woakes to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, England have posted an under-par total on the board and will need to bowl extremely well to defend this one. Sri Lanka will know that this is their game to lose now and they just need to be sensible with the bat and not take unnecessary risk. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Angelo Mathews is up for a chat. He says that it feels good to be back and the fielders complimented the bowlers well here. Adds that he loves to challenge himself and bowling in the past few months has helped him immensely. Mentions that he was well prepared for this chance and it turned out to be good for him and the side. Also adds that they just need to be positive with the chase and play the ball on its merit.

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, was excellent in the field and with the ball as well. Kusal Mendis uses his resources perfectly and the changes that they made for this game turned out to be fruitful. Lahiru Kumara was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets while Angelo Mathews picked up a couple as well. Kasun Rajitha also got two scalps while Maheesh Theekshana finished the job with the last wicket. The catching was brilliant as well and they will be pleased with their effort here. Now, it is up to their batters to complete the task.

A fascinating bowling performance from Sri Lanka as they have restricted England to just 156! This is also the lowest-ever total for England against the Lankans in a World Cup game. The English openers got off to a steady start but both of them failed to convert their starts into big scores. Joe Root failed to make much impact as well as he got run out after a miscommunication with Jonny Bairstow while Jos Buttler's poor form continued. Ben Stokes was their top-scorer with 43 runs but with no real support from the other end, he too could not hang around for much longer and in the end, the defending champions are left staring down the barrel.

OUT! Stamp of humiliation on the English side as Maheesh Theekshana takes the last one. Fuller one, a bit quicker outside off, Mark Wood opts to step out of his crease and go big but fails to get any part of his bat behind this one with Kusal Mendis collecting this behind the wicket and removing the bails in a flash. England are bundled out inside 34 over for just 156 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: The match official and the players take their respective positions. Jos Buttler and Dawid Malan are the two openers for England. Dilshan Madushanka will bowl the first over of this encounter.

We are ready for the pre-match formalities with the match official heading out leading the two sides for their respective National Anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's first, followed by England's National Anthem.

Kusal Mendis, the captain of Sri Lanka says that they would have batted first as the wicket looks good. Adds that he has enough support around him which makes his job easier. Informs Angelo Mathews and Lahiru Kumara come in for this game.

Jos Buttler, the skipper of England says that they will bat first. Adds that the surface looks dry and might spin later also on a used wicket runs on board are key. Mentions that they have been short on performance but they are backing themselves for a good outing today. Also adds that the frustration is there on not playing to their abilities but they have full confidence in each other coming good. Informs they have three changes with Reece Topley ruled out Chris Woakes comes in today. Moeen Ali and Liam Livingstone come in for Gus Atkinson and Harry Brook as they try to balance the side again.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Perera, Kusal Mendis (C/WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, Angelo Mathews (In place of Chamika Karunaratne), Maheesh Theekshana, Kasun Rajitha, Lahiru Kumara (In place of Dushan Hemantha), Dilshan Madushanka.

England (Playing XI) - Jonny Bairstow, Dawid Malan, Joe Root, Ben Stokes, Jos Buttler (C/WK), Liam Livingstone (In place of Harry Brook), Moeen Ali (In place of Gus Atkinson), Chris Woakes (In place of Reece Topley), David Willey, Adil Rashid, Mark Wood.
TOSS - England have won the toss and they elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Ravi Shastri and Dinesh Karthik are out for a pitch report and they say that the pitch is on the drier side and the ball will grip a bit in the second half of the day. The pitch is covered with a bit more grass in the center than near the popping crease. The pitch does have some help on offer for the spinners. The dimensions are even and the surface looks a well-equipped one for the balance of the game.

Sri Lanka managed to gain some momentum with a victory over the Netherlands in their previous game. On the other hand, England will need to regroup after suffering heavy defeats against Afghanistan, South Africa, and New Zealand. The addition of Angelo Mathews in place of Matheesha Pathirana for Sri Lanka means the side now has much me experience, and Brydon Carse for Reece Topley is a like-for-like change for the English side. The match will be a crucial one for both teams as they fight to stay in the tournament. So, who do you think will win this pivotal event? We shall find out together. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Hello and a warm welcome folks! This match between England and Sri Lanka is crucial for both teams as a loss would put them at risk of an early exit. Both teams have struggled with consistent performances and have lost three out of their four games. Injuries to key players like Reece Topley, Dasun Shanaka, Matheesha Pathirana, and Maheesh Theekshana have further weakened the teams. Despite having talented and experienced players, both teams seem to lack the complete package.
...MATCH DAY...

The games continue to come thick and fast in the 2023 ODI World Cup, and match number 25 is upon us, which sees England go up against Sri Lanka at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. The defending champions, England, have had a far-from-ideal start to their title defence, as they currently sit 9th on the points table with only one win from the four games played. Sri Lanka find themselves in a similar position, but they are placed 8th with a solitary win from four matches. After suffering a shock loss against Afghanistan, England were hoping to bounce back, but they were handed a crushing defeat by South Africa. While chasing a humongous target of 400 runs, England could never get going in the chase, and they were rolled over for 170. If Jos Buttler's men are to get their campaign back on track, the batting unit will have to click collectively. The positive for them is that Ben Stokes returned against South Africa, strengthening their batting. Dawid Malan and Joe Root have not had the impact they would have liked, as have Jonny Bairstow and Jos Buttler, who are yet to get a big score. Harry Brook was impressive in the game against Afghanistan but has yet to truly announce his arrival on the big stage. To add to their troubles, left-arm seamer Reece Topley has been ruled out of the competition after fracturing his index finger against South Africa. Brydon Carse has been named as his replacement, but he is unlikely to play against Sri Lanka. With seamers not being that effective in the last outing, England might look at other pace bowling options in Sam Curran or Chris Woakes. On the other hand, Sri Lanka come into this game on the back of a 5-wicket victory against the Netherlands. They restricted the Dutch to 262 and chased it down with 10 balls remaining. Having collected their first points of the tournament, the Asian side will look to build on the momentum created. With Dasun Shanaka already out of the World Cup, Sri Lanka were dealt another injury blow as Matheesha Pathirana's shoulder injury cut his tournament short. Travelled as one of the two reserves, Angelo Mathews has been drafted into the squad as a replacement for the young pacer. Sadeera Samarawickrama and Kusal Mendis have done the heavy lifting, while Pathum Nissanka has returned to form with back-to-back fifties. Kusal Perera and Charith Asalanka have blown hot and cold so far, and they will be hoping to step up with the bat. As they did in the previous encounter, Kasun Rajitha and Dilshan Madushanka will be expected to deal damage with the new ball. Looking at England's struggles against Afghan spinners, ace spinner Maheesh Theekshana will hold the key for Sri Lanka. Although England hold a slight edge over the Asian side in ODIs, the previous three ODI World Cup meetings have been won by Sri Lanka. Who are you backing to come out on top in Bengaluru?
